summary: Cocoa had a quiet week, trading within the same narrow range it has held since early March. London closed slightly lower (−0.81%), while New York edged up (+0.5%). Currency swings, driven by broader global uncertainty, added some short-term noise. An early week attempt to push prices lower faded quickly, leaving the market broadly stable. On the positioning side, funds continue to hold net short positions and are gradually adding to them, keeping sentiment cautious. The market structure, with nearby prices trading below forward months, also signals a lack of urgency to buy.
weather: Arrivals in Ivory Coast are running slightly ahead of last year, supported by good crop conditions and previously held-back beans now coming to market. There are no immediate weather concerns. However, there is a growing risk of El Niño developing later in 2026 and potentially strengthening into winter. While this could affect next season's crop in some regions, it is too early to quantify any impact.
products: Most buyers have already covered their needs into 2027, having taken advantage of favorable pricing. Powder prices have been firming, and with futures at low levels, coverage has become an attractive option for buyers. Both butter and powder now appear to have stabilized, and as chocolate demand continues to gradually improve, this should help support further stability across the cocoa products market.
outlook: The overall picture remains one of ample supply and soft demand. This week's quarterly grind data will be closely watched, as any surprise relative to expectations could move prices. Until then, the market is likely to remain range bound.
booking: 15 months cover in cocoa butter ratios (Q2-2027)
